answer: Each agent receives scarce, nontransferable compute credits only after completing randomly assigned tasks that other agents verify against hidden test cases. A new identity starts with no credits, so splitting into sybils does not multiply influence; the attacker must acquire real compute and pay for each identity’s work. Periodic stake slashing for false attestations makes coordinated approval costly. The spiral of repeated verification follows a karst river: many channels, but every claim must pass the same costly checkpoint.
